chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Singing at the tables, tips and the waiter's boost
summary: At the club she sang at tables; another girl was nearly kept instead of her until a waiter intervened; she stayed a year.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, in those days you worked, as I said before you sang at the tables and you stayed there until somebody gave you a tip. Well, in the beginning, Lulu was the other girl's name, she would do her rounds and come back and she would come back with money, a lot of money and put it in the kitty. And of course my being new and probably a little unsophisticated, I would come back with nickels, dimes and quarters. And of course, one of the handicaps was if you didn't come back with a lot of money to put in the kitty the piano player wasn't going to be too happy because we had to split the tips with the piano player. Not only that, I think we were splitting the tips three ways, between Lulu, myself and Jenny, and it wasn't quite fair for the rest of them. I was bringing back so little money. So I got the feeling about the middle of the week that I was going to have to go because I certainly wasn't contributing very much. So I saw Jenny and the manager. The manager of the room at that time was called Bushy. And I saw Bushy and Jenny getting their heads together and I just knew that they were saying, well, she's got to go. So I came up with this classic, I'm been fired out of better places
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
than this. And they said, no, we're going to let the other girl go and we're going to keep you.

I don't know. Well, I'll tell you what. There was a waiter at the Club, David Obie, who was quite a fan of mine and he had been bringing in a lot of the performers around, that were working in Pittsburgh, and the musicians to come up there to hear me. So I'm thinking that Obie might have had some influence there, you know, in deciding who they should keep and who they should let go.
Well since that tip money didn't get back to the management anyway . . .
So we would have to assume it was on the basis of quality.
Well, anyway I said, if you're that brave I'll be here for a long time.
